authorship: Original Korean example sentences and Japanese explanations, situations and feedback. No quoted source passages.

sources.checked: -ㄹ게 expresses the speaker’s promise or intention to the listener.
Official Korean teaching inventory separately lists -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for plans and for guesses/simple future, plus -(으)ㄹ게요.

Standard promise/intention usage concerns the speaker. Conversational extended third-person usage is not categorically declared impossible; this introductory lesson teaches ordinary first-person promise vs third-person plan.
Primary research compares the intention functions of -겠-, -을 것이-, -을게(요), -을래(요); avoid saying -을 거예요 cannot express intention.
-ㄹ래 states own intention or asks listener intention; lesson contrasts declarative and interrogative uses without rejecting natural invitations.
Official beginner teaching guidance: -ㄹ까요 to discuss what to do together.
KSL grammar training material: -ㄹ까(요) asks conjecture or intention and also functions as proposal; do not translate every use as an invitation.
Both -어서/-니까 can give reasons. Reason -어서 restricted before commands/suggestions; apology/thanks commonly use -어서. Restriction not generalized to sequential -어서.
-지마는 / short form -지만 acknowledges earlier fact then adds an opposing/different fact.
-는데 can give background before explanation, question, command, suggestion.
Primary study of connective -는데 distinguishes background/explanation and unexpected or contrary developments; not always contrast.

pedagogy: Learn two complete examples and their original audio before answering Japanese meaning/situation choices.
Do not force spontaneous versus previously planned decisions; both forms can convey intention, and context can make -을 거예요 a promise.
Use listener-directed offer/promise, explaining a plan, and describing another person’s planned attendance. Do not teach categorical prohibition of conversational extended forms.
35-2: own preference vs listener willingness, two valid invitations, offer vs conjecture.
35-3: reason for an event vs advice, apology vs next action, both causal endings in a reported past action. Do not teach absolute objective/subjective split.
35-4: both forms can contrast; -는데 also gives background and a context-dependent indirect response, not always refusal.
